Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt

many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until

p='programs/task-ce7b257f.py'
open(p,'w').write('''def transform(grid):
    # Each patterned patch contains a colored marker; propagate its color into
    # the 2x2 interior of every 4x4 motif of the same large tiled region.
    g=[r[:] for r in grid]
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    # identify the color-1 connected components and marker colors within each
    # patch; local motif geometry is periodic, color spread based on marker.
    # markers define palette for groups of recurring motifs, inferred per regions.
    # Apply marker color to 2x2 interior blocks within each component's bbox,
    # where motifs have 1-cell border and 2x2 center.
    seen=set(); comps=[]
    for i in range(h):
      for j in range(w):
       if g[i][j]==1 and (i,j) not in seen:
        st=[(i,j)]; seen.add((i,j)); cells=[]
        while st:
         r,c=st.pop(); cells.append((r,c))
         for dr,dc in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
          q=(r+dr,c+dc)
          if 0<=q[0]<h and 0<=q[1]<w and g[q[0]][q[1]]==1 and q not in seen: seen.add(q); st.append(q)
        comps.append(cells)
    # Detect periodic 4x4 motifs by marker-containing region; marker color fills
    # matching 2x2 centers.
    markers=[(i,j,v) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if (v:=g[i][j]) not in (0,1)]
    for mr,mc,col in markers:
      # region defined by nearby connected foreground component (including marker)
      # For each marker, discover 4x4 lattice center alignment from its location.
      # center positions are marker coordinate modulo four; fill same-aligned centers
      # across component's local extent.
      comp=next((x for x in comps if any(abs(r-mr)<=2 and abs(c-mc)<=2 for r,c in x)),None)
      if comp is None: continue
      r0=min(r for r,c in comp); r1=max(r for r,c in comp); c0=min(c for r,c in comp); c1=max(c for r,c in comp)
      # use marker as center of its 2x2 motif when possible; marked location aligns within center
      ar=mr%4; ac=mc%4
      # phase centers from marker at row/col position within periodic arrangement
      for r in range(r0,r1+1):
       for c in range(c0,c1+1):
        if (r%4 in ((mr-1)%4,mr%4) and c%4 in ((mc-1)%4,mc%4) and g[r][c]==1): g[r][c]=col
    return g
''')

    g=[row[:] for row in grid]
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    # Background cells enclosed inside a foreground object's bounding box are
    # filled using the marker color belonging to that object's component.
    markers=[(r,c,g[r][c]) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if g[r][c] not in (0,1)]
    seen=set()
    for r in range(h):
      for c in range(w):
        if grid[r][c]!=1 or (r,c) in seen: continue
        stack=[(r,c)]; comp=[]; seen.add((r,c))
        while stack:
          x,y=stack.pop();comp.append((x,y))
          for dx,dy in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
            nx,ny=x+dx,y+dy
            if 0<=nx<h and 0<=ny<w and grid[nx][ny]==1 and (nx,ny) not in seen:
              seen.add((nx,ny));stack.append((nx,ny))
        nearby=[(a,b,col) for a,b,col in markers if any(abs(a-x)+abs(b-y)<=1 for x,y in comp)]
        if not nearby: continue
        mr,mc,col=min(nearby,key=lambda z:min(abs(z[0]-x)+abs(z[1]-y) for x,y in comp))
        r0=min(x for x,y in comp);r1=max(x for x,y in comp);c0=min(y for x,y in comp);c1=max(y for x,y in comp)
        for x in range(r0,r1+1):
          for y in range(c0,c1+1):

    return g
''')
